title: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT)
subject: haematology-oncology
setting: Ward, ICU, cardiac surgery, dialysis unit
summary: Calculate the 4Ts score; if intermediate or high, stop all heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant (argatroban, bivalirudin, fondaparinux or a DOAC) while testing for PF4/heparin antibodies. Avoid warfarin until platelets recover and avoid routine platelet transfusion.

sections.title: Suspect HIT and score it
items: Typical pattern: platelet fall of more than 50% (nadir usually 20 to 100 x 10^9/L) 5 to 10 days after starting heparin; within 24 hours if heparin was given in the previous 30 days.
Clues: new venous or arterial thrombosis, skin necrosis at injection sites, or an acute systemic reaction after an IV heparin bolus. Bleeding is uncommon.
4Ts score, Thrombocytopenia: fall above 50% and nadir 20 or more = 2; fall 30 to 50% or nadir 10 to 19 = 1; fall below 30% or nadir below 10 = 0.

4Ts score, Timing of fall: day 5 to 10, or 1 day or less with heparin in the past 30 days = 2; probable but unclear, after day 10, or 1 day or less with exposure 30 to 100 days ago = 1; before day 4 without recent exposure = 0.

4Ts score, Thrombosis: new proven thrombosis, skin necrosis or systemic reaction = 2; progressive, recurrent or suspected thrombosis = 1; none = 0. oTher cause for thrombocytopenia: none apparent = 2; possible = 1; definite = 0. Total 0 to 3 low, 4 to 5 intermediate, 6 to 8 high probability.
Risk is highest with UFH after surgery (especially cardiac surgery), intermediate with UFH in medical patients, low with LMWH in medical patients and negligible with fondaparinux.

sections.title: Testing (ASH 2018)
items: Low 4Ts (0 to 3): do not send HIT tests and do not treat as HIT; look for other causes (sepsis, DIC, drugs, haemodilution, bypass).
Intermediate or high 4Ts: PF4/heparin immunoassay (ELISA: a low optical density threshold is preferred); if positive, a functional assay (SRA or HIPA) where available.
Negative immunoassay: stop the non-heparin anticoagulant and resume heparin if indicated.
Isolated HIT: bilateral leg compression ultrasound to look for silent proximal DVT, and ultrasound of any arm with a central venous catheter.
Baseline APTT, PT/INR, fibrinogen, liver function and creatinine clearance to guide the choice of anticoagulant.

sections.title: Immediate management (intermediate or high 4Ts)
items: Stop ALL heparin: UFH, LMWH, heparin flushes, heparin-locked lines and heparin in dialysis circuits. Label the chart clearly.

Start a non-heparin anticoagulant at therapeutic intensity. Exception: intermediate 4Ts, high bleeding risk and no other indication for full anticoagulation: prophylactic intensity until results return.

Critically ill, high bleeding risk or likely procedures: argatroban or bivalirudin (short acting). Stable with average bleeding risk: fondaparinux or a DOAC (most experience with rivaroxaban). Life- or limb-threatening thrombosis: parenteral agent.
If on warfarin at diagnosis: stop it and give vitamin K 5 to 10 mg IV, while starting the non-heparin anticoagulant (warfarin in acute HIT can cause venous limb gangrene).
Do not give routine platelet transfusions; reserve for active bleeding or a high-risk procedure. Do not insert an IVC filter routinely.

sections.title: Non-heparin anticoagulant dosing
items: Argatroban: 2 mcg/kg/min IV, no bolus; 0.5 to 1.2 mcg/kg/min if bilirubin above 1.5 mg/dL, heart failure, anasarca or after cardiac surgery. Titrate to APTT 1.5 to 3.0 times baseline. Suitable in renal failure; avoid or reduce in Child-Pugh B or C liver disease.
Bivalirudin: 0.15 mg/kg/hour IV, no bolus; APTT 1.5 to 2.5 times baseline; dose reduction may be needed in renal or hepatic dysfunction.
Fondaparinux SC once daily: below 50 kg 5 mg, 50 to 100 kg 7.5 mg, above 100 kg 10 mg. Avoid if CrCl below 30 mL/min.
Rivaroxaban: HIT with thrombosis 15 mg twice daily for 3 weeks then 20 mg once daily; isolated HIT 15 mg twice daily until platelet recovery.

Apixaban: HIT with thrombosis 10 mg twice daily for 7 days then 5 mg twice daily; isolated HIT 5 mg twice daily until platelet recovery. Dabigatran 150 mg twice daily only after 5 days or more of a parenteral agent (HIT with thrombosis).
Argatroban, bivalirudin, fondaparinux, rivaroxaban and apixaban are available in India; fondaparinux or rivaroxaban are practical for stable patients.

sections.title: Duration and transition
items: Isolated HIT: anticoagulate at least until platelets recover (usually 150 x 10^9/L or more), and not beyond 3 months unless the count has not recovered.
HIT with thrombosis: anticoagulate for 3 to 6 months.

Once platelets have recovered, a DOAC is preferred over warfarin. If warfarin is used, start only after platelet recovery and overlap with the non-heparin agent for at least 5 days and until the INR is therapeutic (argatroban also raises the INR).
Document heparin allergy (HIT) with the date in the records and discharge summary; advise an alert card or bracelet for 3 months.

sections.title: Special situations
items: Cardiac surgery: delay until antibodies have cleared if possible; otherwise bivalirudin, or intraoperative heparin after plasma exchange, in expert centres.
PCI in acute HIT: bivalirudin (argatroban if unavailable).
Renal replacement therapy in acute HIT: argatroban or bivalirudin for the circuit; in remote HIT regional citrate is suggested.
Remote HIT needing VTE prophylaxis or treatment: use a non-heparin agent (fondaparinux, DOAC or warfarin) rather than UFH or LMWH.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Testing and treating patients with a low 4Ts score: HIT is overdiagnosed.
Stopping heparin without starting an alternative anticoagulant: thrombotic risk remains high and delays cost about 6% per day in new thrombosis, amputation or death.
Starting warfarin during acute thrombocytopenia.
Forgetting heparin flushes, heparin-coated catheters and dialysis heparin.

drugs.name: Argatroban
drugs.dose: 2 mcg/kg/min IV infusion, no bolus (0.5 to 1.2 mcg/kg/min in hepatic dysfunction, heart failure, anasarca or post cardiac surgery)
drugs.notes: Target APTT 1.5 to 3.0 times baseline. Hepatic clearance.

drugs.name: Bivalirudin
drugs.notes: Target APTT 1.5 to 2.5 times baseline. Reduce in renal or hepatic dysfunction.

drugs.name: Fondaparinux (treatment dose)
drugs.dose: SC once daily: below 50 kg 5 mg; 50 to 100 kg 7.5 mg; above 100 kg 10 mg

drugs.name: Rivaroxaban
drugs.dose: HITT: 15 mg orally twice daily for 3 weeks, then 20 mg once daily. Isolated HIT: 15 mg twice daily until platelet recovery
drugs.notes: For clinically stable patients at average bleeding risk.

drugs.name: Apixaban
drugs.dose: HITT: 10 mg orally twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily. Isolated HIT: 5 mg twice daily until platelet recovery
drugs.notes: For clinically stable patients at average bleeding risk.

drugs.name: Dabigatran
drugs.notes: HITT: only after at least 5 days of a parenteral non-heparin anticoagulant.

drugs.name: Vitamin K (phytomenadione)
drugs.notes: If on warfarin when HIT is diagnosed.
